approved: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Regulatory Levies) Amendment Bill 2013
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would let a government body collect an annual fee from companies that hold certain offshore oil and gas permits.
It changes an existing law to cover permits obtained through a cash bidding system, where companies pay a lump sum for the right to explore.
The bill aims to recover the full cost of the administrator's work, and the government says it will not affect the budget.
Adds cash bid petroleum exploration permits to the list of titles subject to the annual administration levy.
Allows the National Offshore Petroleum Titles Administrator to collect that levy for those permits.
Makes consequential amendments to support full cost recovery for the administrator.
Companies holding cash bid petroleum exploration permits in Australia's offshore oil and gas areas.

Referred the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Amendment (Cash Bidding) Bill 2013 and the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Regulatory Levies) Amendment Bill 2013 to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

Supported the offshore petroleum cash bidding bill, explaining its two-stage process assessing an applicant's suitability before allowing a cash bid for exploration permits, said unsuccessful bidders who withdraw would forfeit a 10 per cent deposit, and welcomed the added transparency and fairness this brings to permit allocation.

Argued that separating bidder prequalification from cash bids ensures offshore petroleum permits are judged on price alone once safety and financial capacity are assessed, and welcomed the reserve price and 10 per cent deposit forfeiture as protecting the value of Australia's hydrocarbon assets.

Closed debate on the cash bidding bills, explaining that a 10 per cent deposit will discourage frivolous bids and that unsuccessful bidders can appeal under the Administrative Decisions (Judicial Review) Act, and confirmed the National Offshore Petroleum Titles Administrator will recover its annual titles administration costs through the new levy.
